1.scope: Public discovery, author workspace, admin operations, storage, cache, background jobs and exclusions from v1 scope.

2.scope: Guest visibility, Author/Admin role restrictions, ownership and verified author policy.

3.scope: Recipe, category and child data business model. See subsections for invariants.

3.1.scope: Aggregate children, ordering, six nutrition fields, references and mutation transaction, validation, authorization and cache invalidation.

3.2.scope: Draft, Published and Archived transitions; visibility; idempotent publish/unpublish; active children; stable published slug.

3.3.scope: Draft creation, field validation, category, unique slug suffix, atomic aggregate and publication effects.

3.4.scope: Public reads, admin writes, stable slug, referenced recipe conflict, soft deletion and active-only slug uniqueness.

3.5.scope: Owner/Admin, 5 MB, JPEG/PNG/WebP/AVIF, magic bytes, GUID object paths, primary replacement and image variants.

3.6.scope: Child validation, nullable fields, bounds, access, ETags, soft delete, atomic reorder, step images and public DTO compatibility.

3.7.scope: Two-stage deletion, storage retention, cache invalidation, purge, active slug uniqueness and optimistic concurrency.

4.scope: Vietnamese search, relevance and filters, sorting and paging contracts, cache TTL, invalidation and Redis fallback.

5.scope: Password hashing, Google ID token, role assignment, JWT claims/TTL and memory storage, hashed rotating refresh cookies, logout and rate limits.

6.scope: Versioned routes, authorization, request/response DTOs, wrappers, Problem Details and all listed operations. Review endpoint inventory alongside this section.

7.scope: Deployment topology and layer boundaries. Detailed responsibilities in the following subsections.

7.1.scope: Dependency Rule, layer responsibilities, Domain package restriction, composition root and OpenAPI/Scalar.

7.2.scope: Logging, validation, query caching, handler execution, command invalidation and read/write separation.

7.3.scope: Frontend architecture and acceptance requirements in subsections 7.3.1 through 7.3.6.

7.3.1.scope: Server and Client Component boundaries, query and client state, form validation and separate internal/public API origins.

7.3.2.scope: Historical package snapshot and the pending single session authority decision. Review current dependencies and Auth.js/JWT ownership.

7.3.3.scope: Target routes, server render/ISR, interactive dashboards, URL state, permissions and SEO visibility.

7.3.4.scope: DTO consistency, category detail endpoint, development-only fallbacks, token storage, credentialed refresh, route guards and container API origins.

7.3.5.scope: Shared layout, optimized images/fonts, mobile navigation, focus and ARIA, newsletter scope and SEO metadata.

7.3.6.scope: API client boundaries, typed DTOs, query keys, URL filters, private cache and token isolation, UI states and test scope.

7.4.scope: Data types, nullability, constraints, relationship and cascade rules, filtered indexes, concurrency and PostgreSQL FTS.

7.5.scope: Compose, TLS, volumes, backups, secrets, health probes, structured logs, tracing and business metrics.

8.scope: Latency, load, cache, query efficiency, frontend performance, security, accessibility, availability, retry, error contract, tests and SEO.

10.scope: Normalized decisions on deletion, slug indexes, sorting, nullable ingredients, nutrition, steps, cache, Google OAuth, token storage and error codes.

11.scope: Suggested implementation order for the already mapped requirements.

12.scope: Each checklist item is mapped below by its text and checked against the source.
